findings.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar), so all other hosts' destination calendars for a COLLECTIVE booking are silently dropped with no error, defeating the PR's stated purpose

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar` from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can be undefined (empty array/null), but `.integration` is accessed without optional chaining, throwing TypeError where the old code safely used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72 — Office365CalendarService.createEvent` was not updated to accept the new `credentialId: number` param required by the `Calendar` interface, so `CalendarManager.createEvent`'s `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` silently drops credentialId and this implementer always uses `destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which host/credential is invoked

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 — LarkCalendarService.createEvent` was not updated to accept the new `credentialId: number` param required by the `Calendar` interface, so it always resolves the calendar via `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of the credential-matched entry, defeating the multi-host destinationCalendar fix for this provider

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 — BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (CalDAV base class) was not updated to accept the new `credentialId: number` param required by the `Calendar` interface; `credentialId` passed by `CalendarManager.createEvent` is silently ignored and only `destinationCalendar[0]` is ever used

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (no eventType/organizer destinationCalendar), so collective team members' destination calendars are silently dropped instead of being added

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — Calendar interface widened to createEvent(event, credentialId) but only GoogleCalendarService (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:101) actually uses credentialId to pick a destinationCalendar entry; LarkCalendarService (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125) and Office365CalendarService (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72) keep the old single-arg signature and always use destinationCalendar[0], so the same interface method is honored inconsistently across implementers and multi-host writes collapse onto one host's calendar for non-Google providers.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — evt.destinationCalendar falls back to null here while every other construction site in this diff (handleCancelBooking.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule/deleteCredential handlers, bookingReminder.ts) falls back to []; the very next block (line 1078) does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), which silently no-ops when null, dropping team hosts' destination calendars exactly in the COLLECTIVE case this PR is meant to fix.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — The `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = X.destinationCalendar ?? []` one-liner is copy-pasted 11 times across 6 files (EventManager.ts, GoogleCalendarService.ts x2, LarkCalendarService.ts x4, Office365CalendarService.ts, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts x2, BrokenIntegrationEmail.tsx); this is the only one of the 11 that drops the optional-chaining safety (`mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` instead of `?.integration`) that all the other copies keep, so it will throw when destinationCalendar is empty/undefined — the duplicated pattern has already drifted out of sync.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:342 — The "fetch credential from DB when not in this.calendarCredentials, then hand-reconstruct a partial {appName,id,type,key,userId,teamId,invalid,appId} object" block is duplicated verbatim in createAllCalendarEvents (line 342-368) and updateAllCalendarEvents (line 517-541), and a third, structurally different copy exists in handleCancelBooking.ts:433 that skips the `include: { app: { select: { slug } } }` / app.slug-required guard and assigns the raw Prisma Credential record directly; a future fix to this fallback logic (e.g. the app.slug guard) is unlikely to be applied to all three copies.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:70 — this.calendarCredentials, built once in the constructor as "the credentials this EventManager has," is no longer a reliable source of truth: createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents both now routinely bypass it with ad hoc prisma.credential.findUnique fallback fetches when a referenced credentialId isn't found in the constructor-populated array, indicating the class's credential-management responsibility is no longer well encapsulated.

packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts:26 — destinationCalendar was mechanically retyped from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[]|null with no normalization logic added to setDestinationCalendar (builder.ts:198) or the builder's user/team-aware methods; this second, independent CalendarEvent-construction path (parallel to the object literal in handleNewBooking.ts) was not updated to collect multiple hosts' destinationCalendars, so any existing caller still passing a single DestinationCalendar object through this builder silently reintroduces the old single-object shape.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — The field kept its singular name (destinationCalendar) despite becoming an array everywhere in this diff; this naming leak is a plausible root cause of several concrete bugs found elsewhere in the same diff (the null-vs-[] fallback inconsistency in handleNewBooking.ts, and the missing optional chaining in EventManager.ts), since readers/writers keep instinctively treating it like a single nullable object.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 — Unlike every sibling handler in this diff (handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts), which all fall back to `... || user.destinationCalendar` before defaulting to [], this call site was simplified to only use bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar with no user-level fallback, breaking the otherwise-consistent convention established across the rest of the diff.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

However, that behavior is an intentional robustness measure (handling credential IDs not present in the constructor-provided list), and the proposed finding frames it as an encapsulation/design concern (“no longer well encapsulated”, “not reliable source of truth”) rather than a concrete bug/correctness/security defect. Nothing in the diff demonstrates incorrect behavior resulting from this fallback; it still uses `this.calendarCredentials` when available and only falls back when missing. So the finding is not a verifiable problem in the sense required.
